title: Pembrolizumab with cisplatin and definitive cervical chemoradiotherapy

page_map.1: Adult FIGO 2014 stage III–IVA, previously untreated definitively. EBRT then brachytherapy. Schedule, clinically stable initial progression and 24-month limit. No CPS eligibility threshold.
page_map.2: Concurrent administration order, cisplatin radiation-day coordination, optional C2D15, hydration and cycles 3–5.
page_map.3: Cycles 6–20, ECOG 2 discretion, exclusions and cautions.
page_map.5: Table 3 organ impairment, Table 4 cisplatin neuropathy, Table 5 pulmonary, gastrointestinal and renal immune toxicity.
page_map.6: Table 5 endocrine, hepatic, skin, other immune and infusion toxicity, recurrent events, 12-week stop and steroid-taper criteria.
page_map.7: High emetogenic risk with cisplatin, minimal with pembrolizumab. Interaction checks and HPRA patient card.

decisions: The summary cites Table 4 for pembrolizumab toxicity; the printed immune toxicity table is Table 5 (pp5–6). Source table headings and contents govern the mapping.

Schedule and code follow the national PDF. The national website displays the parent regimen number. No optional sixth cisplatin dose without a consultant decision. Long-course pembrolizumab remains inside this definitive protocol.

A raw raised creatinine, AST/ALT or bilirubin requires assessment of immune causality and other causes. The protocol uses ULN-based cutoffs for immune nephritis/hepatitis, independently of absolute creatinine clearance for cisplatin.
Unresolved fractional cisplatin clearance bands need review. Dialysis is a separate discretionary pathway. A cisplatin-specific adjustment is never applied automatically to pembrolizumab.
